title: Ogee Spillway Discharge

C₀.description: Discharge coefficient (≈2.18 m^0.5/s at design head for WES profile)

He.description: Total energy head on crest = h + Va²/(2g)

applicability: C₀ varies with He/Hd (0.6–1.06×C₀_design), P/Hd (approach depth effect), and downstream submergence. US customary: C₀ ≈ 3.95 ft^0.5/s at design head.
source: USBR Design of Small Dams (1987), USACE HDC 111-1 to 111-9

title: WES Ogee Crest Profile (Downstream)

x.description: Horizontal distance downstream from crest apex (positive downstream)

y.description: Vertical distance below crest apex (negative = below crest)

Hd.description: Design head (head at which crest shape is designed)

applicability: Profile follows the lower nappe of a sharp-crested weir at Hd. Upstream face uses circular arcs tangent to the upstream dam face.
source: USBR Design of Small Dams, USACE HDC 111-2

title: Effective Crest Length (Pier and Abutment Correction)
source: USBR Design of Small Dams, USACE HDC 111-5

title: Cavitation Index

Pv.description: Vapor pressure of water (≈2.3 kPa at 20°C)

applicability: σ < 0.2: cavitation damage likely. σ < 0.1: severe damage. Cavitation concern begins at V > 12 m/s (40 ft/s). Surface offsets > 6 mm can trigger cavitation at high velocities.
source: Falvey (1990) Cavitation in Chutes and Spillways — USBR EM 42

title: Hydraulic Jump Sequent Depth (Stilling Basin)
applicability: For rectangular basins. Tailwater depth must equal or slightly exceed y₂ to hold the jump in the basin. If TW < y₂: jump sweeps out. If TW >> y₂: submerged jump (less efficient).

title: Stilling Basin Length (Empirical)
source: USBR EM 25 — Hydraulic Design of Stilling Basins

title: Flip Bucket (Ski Jump) Trajectory

θ.description: Flip bucket lip angle above horizontal

applicability: Projectile equations. Actual throw is less than theoretical due to air resistance and jet breakup. Typical lip angles: 20°–45°.
source: General hydraulics — USBR Design of Small Dams

title: Scour Depth Below Flip Bucket (Mason & Arumugam)

d_particle.description: Mean rock block size in plunge pool

applicability: Empirical. Multiple formulas exist (Veronese, Mason, Bollaert). Results vary widely — use multiple methods and engineering judgment.

title: Labyrinth Weir Discharge

Cd.description: Discharge coefficient (function of Ht/P, L/W, sidewall angle, crest shape)

L.description: Total developed crest length (sum of all weir segments)

applicability: At low Ht/P (<0.3): Cd approaches flat plate weir value (~0.60). At high Ht/P (>0.7): efficiency drops as adjacent nappes interfere. Design typically for Ht/P ≤ 0.6–0.8.

title: Stepped Spillway Energy Dissipation
alt_form: Simplified: Residual energy fraction ≈ 1 - 0.6 to 0.85 of total head (depending on dam height and unit discharge)

ΔE/E₀.description: Fraction of total energy dissipated on steps

f_friction.description: Darcy-Weisbach friction factor on steps (0.1–0.2 for skimming flow)

applicability: For skimming flow regime. Energy dissipation increases with number of steps (dam height) and decreases with increasing unit discharge.

title: Air Entrainment Bulking Factor

C_air.description: Average air concentration in flow (0.20–0.40 typical on steep chutes)

applicability: Self-aeration begins when turbulent boundary layer reaches the free surface. For chute wall and freeboard design, use bulked depth. C_air depends on slope, velocity, and roughness.

title: Morning Glory (Shaft) Spillway — Crest-Controlled Discharge
equation: Q = C₀ × π × D × H^1.5  (crest-controlled, unsubmerged)
applicability: Three flow regimes: crest-controlled (free weir flow, low H), tube-controlled (orifice flow, moderate H), and pipe-controlled (full conduit, high H). Transitions between regimes create unstable discharge characteristics — careful design required.
source: USBR Design of Small Dams, Wagner (1956)
